football_evidence.question: Can Washington contain Nebraska’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.3 points.
supporting: When Nebraska has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Nebraska’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 20.3% of its runs, and Washington’s defense stops 25.0% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
In his last two games (Indiana and Oregon), Colandrea averaged 5.4 yards per attempt, against 8.2 in his five games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Washington’s receivers No. 13 nationally and Nebraska’s No. 61.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Washington’s linebackers No. 6 nationally and Nebraska’s No. 56.
contradicting: When Nebraska has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Nebraska’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.8% of its dropbacks, and Washington’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Washington has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Washington’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.9% of its dropbacks, and Nebraska’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When Washington has the ball (third down): Washington’s offense converts 34.5% of its third downs, and Nebraska’s defense allows opponents to convert 16.3% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Washington has the ball (the red zone): Washington’s offense succeeds on 44.8% of its red-zone plays, and Nebraska’s defense allows success on 26.7% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
quarterbacks: Anthony Colandrea has completed 137 of 223 passes (61.4%) for 1,601 yards, 7.2 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in seven games for Nebraska, and has been sacked on 13 of 236 dropbacks.

Demond Williams Jr. has completed 114 of 174 passes (65.5%) for 1,386 yards, 8.0 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for Washington, and has been sacked on 18 of 192 dropbacks.
Elijah Brown has completed 51 of 70 passes (72.9%) for 578 yards, 8.3 yards per attempt, 7 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in three games for Washington, and has been sacked on 3 of 73 dropbacks.
